newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU clears Ford service outlet deal.
newsitem.headline: EU clears Ford service outlet deal.

text.p: The European Commission said on Monday it had approved a service outlet agreement of U.S. car giant Ford which will be implemented in all European Union member states with the exception of Britain.

The agreement provides that the smallest Ford dealers, who mainly do servicing and sell only some 30 to 50 cars a year, will cease to be network dealers and instead become service outlets, the Commission said in a statement.

"As service outlets, they will concentrate on providing maintenance, repair and warranty services to Ford customers," it said. The agreement would be concluded between the service outlet and the dealer to which the outlet is linked.

The service outlets would have no legal obligation to sell cars. "The service outlets are free to sell and service cars of other (brands) and to use spare parts of matching quality, except in the case of warranty work," the Commission said.
The Commission said the agreement falls within the scope of EU rules banning deals which prevent, distort or restrict competition.
However, it decided to approve the agreement, partly as it offers consumers the advantage of retaining a service near home, of special importance for those living in remote areas.
Ford notified the agreement to the Commission in June last year.
